items.title: Item 4
items.text: Berkshire Hathaway’s Portfolio Shakeup ***************************************** Berkshire Hathaway (NYSE:BRKB ) revealed significant changes to its stock portfolio on Friday, marking the first full quarter under new CEO Greg Abel. According to a regulatory filing, the conglomerate acquired a $2.6 billion stake in Delta Air Lines (NYSE:DAL ), returning to a stock it previously exited in 2020. Berkshire also added a $55 million stake in Macy’s (NYSE:M ) and bought nearly 40 million additional shares of Alphabet (NASDAQ:GOOG ). * Chevron (NYSE:CVX ) stake cut by $2.4 billion: Abel also reduced Berkshire’s Bank of America (NYSE:BAC ) holding by $3.4 billion. And he exited UnitedHealth (NYSE:UNH ) – which subsequently fell around 4% in pre-market trading – along with Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN ), Domino’s Pizza (NASDAQ:DPZ ), Mastercard (NYSE:MA ), and Visa (NYSE:V ), which were all relatively small holdings. * Maintaining a concentrated approach to investing: Abel, who took over in January, noted at Berkshire's recent annual meeting that he and Warren Buffett still collaborate on stock purchases – and he left Berkshire’s big stake in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL ) unchanged.
